title: Events as sets
objectives: Combine events with union, intersection and complement.
Read “or”, “and” and “not” as set operations, and count the regions.

screens.prose: A Venn diagram sorts the same 36 rolls into four regions. Each number counts the rolls in its region. Tap a region to select it.
screens.question: Tap every region that lies inside $A$.

hints.text: $A$ is the whole left circle, overlap included.
The overlap is inside the left circle too.

feedback.correct: $A$ is the whole left circle: $9 + 9 = 18$ rolls.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Select every part of the left circle.

byKey.a-only: You tapped only the part of $A$ outside $B$. The overlap is inside $A$ too.
byKey.B: That region is $B$ without $A$: rolls with an odd red die.
byKey.none: That region is outside both circles.
byKey.AB: You missed the overlap. Rolls in both events are still in $A$.

explain.text: $A$ is the whole left circle: 9 rolls in $A$ only and 9 in the overlap. That makes $|A| = 18$, the three even rows of the grid.

screens.prose: Your 9 rolls from the grid sit in the overlap: in $A$ **and** in $B$. That region is the **intersection**, $A \cap B$. Rolls in $A$ **or** $B$, including both, form the **union**, $A \cup B$.
screens.question: Tap every region of $A \cup B$.

hints.text: A roll is in $A \cup B$ if it is in at least one of the circles.
This region is in both, so it is in at least one.
Select all three regions inside the circles.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Select every region inside at least one circle.

byKey.xor: You left out the overlap. “Or” includes rolls in both.
byKey.and: That is $A \cap B$, both at once. The union needs only one of them.
byKey.none: The outside region holds rolls in neither event.

explain.text: $A \cup B$ is everything inside either circle: $9 + 9 + 6 = 24$ rolls. $A \cap B$ is only the overlap, 9 rolls. In probability, “or” always includes both.

screens.prose: The rolls where $A$ does **not** happen form the **complement** of $A$, written $A^c$. Here $A^c$ means the red die is odd.
screens.question: Tap every region of $A^c$.

hints.text: $A^c$ is everything outside the left circle.
This region is outside the left circle.
Select the part of $B$ outside $A$, and the region outside both.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Select every region outside the left circle.

byKey.outside: You tapped only the outside. Rolls in $B$ but not $A$ are also outside $A$.
byKey.b-only: You missed the outside region. Rolls in neither event are not in $A$ either.

explain.text: $A^c$ is everything outside the left circle: $6 + 12 = 18$ rolls. $A$ and $A^c$ cover all 36 rolls with no overlap: $18 + 18 = 36$.

screens.prose: The shaded region is “neither $A$ nor $B$”: outside both circles. That is the complement of the union, $(A \cup B)^c$.
screens.question: Which other expression names the same region?

options.why: You took both complements but kept the union. $A^c \cup B^c$ also holds $A$ only and $B$ only.
That removes only the overlap. It still holds $A$ only and $B$ only.
$A^c$ also holds $B$ only. “Neither” means outside $B$ too.

hints.text: “Neither” means not in $A$, and also not in $B$.
Where is $A^c$? Where is $B^c$? Find where they meet.
$A^c$ is outside the left circle and $B^c$ outside the right. Both hold only in the outside region.

feedback.correct: Not in $A$ and not in $B$: the outside region.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shade $A^c$ and $B^c$ in your head, and find where both hold.

explain.text: Not in $A$ and not in $B$ is the same as not in $A \cup B$: $(A \cup B)^c = A^c \cap B^c$. Likewise $(A \cap B)^c = A^c \cup B^c$. These are **De Morgan's laws**: a complement swaps $\cup$ and $\cap$.

screens.prose: New events. $A$: the total is 7. $B$: the dice match, a double.
screens.question: What is $P(A \cup B)$? Give a fraction or a decimal.

hints.text: Can a double total 7?
The overlap is empty.
A double totals 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 or 12, never 7. So $|A \cup B| = 6 + 6$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the rolls in either circle, then divide by 36.

byKey.subtract: You took away an overlap of 1. No double totals 7, so the overlap is empty.
byKey.one: That is one event alone. The union holds the rolls of both.
byKey.both: That is $P(A \cap B)$, which is 0 here. The union holds 12 rolls.

explain.text: A double always has an even total, so no roll is in both: $A \cap B = \varnothing$. Events like these are **disjoint**, and their counts simply add: $\tfrac{6 + 6}{36} = \tfrac{1}{3}$.

screens.prose: Back to $A$, red die even, and $B$, total 8 or more. A bet pays if $A$ or $B$ happens. Jo counts the paying rolls as $9 + 6 = 15$.
screens.question: On how many of the 36 rolls does the bet pay?

hints.text: Does the bet pay on a roll that is in both $A$ and $B$?
Jo left this region out.
Add all three regions inside the circles: $9 + 9 + 6$.

feedback.correct: All three regions inside the circles: 24 rolls.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The bet pays on every roll inside either circle.

byKey.xor: You counted Jo's way and left out the overlap. “Or” includes rolls in both, so add the 9 there.
byKey.double: You added $|A| = 18$ and $|B| = 15$. The 9 overlap rolls are in both, so you counted them twice.
byKey.and: That is $A \cap B$. The bet also pays on rolls in just one event.
byKey.all: The 12 rolls outside both circles do not pay.

explain.text: In probability “or” is inclusive, so the bet pays in all three regions: $9 + 9 + 6 = 24$ rolls. Adding $|A| + |B| = 33$ counts the overlap twice, so take it away once: $33 - 9 = 24$. So $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac{24}{36} = \tfrac{2}{3}$.

screens.prose: Your fix was to take the overlap away once. Let us turn that into a rule for any two events $A$ and $B$.
screens.question: Put the lines of the argument in order.

lines.text: $|A \cup B| = |A \text{ only}| + |A \cap B| + |B \text{ only}|$: three regions that do not overlap.
$|A| + |B| = |A \text{ only}| + 2|A \cap B| + |B \text{ only}|$: the overlap sits in both circles.
Subtract the two lines: $|A \cup B| = |A| + |B| - |A \cap B|$.
Divide by $|S|$: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$.

hints.text: Start by splitting the union into its regions.
Then compare that with what $|A| + |B|$ counts: this region is in both circles.
Union first, then $|A| + |B|$, then subtract, then divide by $|S|$.

feedback.correct: The overlap is counted twice, so it comes off once.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write both counts in terms of the three regions before you subtract.

explain.text: $|A| + |B|$ counts the overlap twice, so we subtract it once. Dividing by $|S|$ turns counts into chances when outcomes are equally likely. The full rule, for any chances, comes later in the course.

screens.prose: Twenty trading days of one stock. Event $A$: it closes above £50. Event $B$: volume is above 1 million shares.

state.caption: $A$: close above £50. $B$: volume above 1 million shares.

screens.question: On how many of the 20 days did $A$ or $B$ happen?

hints.text: Count the $A$ days, the $B$ days, and the days with both.
These five days had both.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count $|A|$, $|B|$ and $|A \cap B|$, then take the overlap away once.

byKey.double: You added 11 and 8. The 5 days with both were counted twice.
byKey.xor: You counted days with exactly one event. Days with both count too.
byKey.and: That is $A \cap B$. The union also holds days with just one event.
byKey.neither: That is the days in neither event, $(A \cup B)^c$. Take it from 20.

explain.text: 11 days closed above £50 and 8 had high volume, but 5 days had both. So $|A \cup B| = 11 + 8 - 5 = 14$, and on this sample $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac{14}{20} = 0.7$. The other 6 days are $A^c \cap B^c$.

ideas: “And” is the intersection $A \cap B$, “or” is the union $A \cup B$, and “not” is the complement $A^c$.
“Or” includes both. Adding $|A| + |B|$ counts the overlap twice, so take it away once.
De Morgan: $(A \cup B)^c = A^c \cap B^c$ and $(A \cap B)^c = A^c \cup B^c$.

formula.name: Union by counting
formula.note: Disjoint events have $A \cap B = \varnothing$, so their counts simply add.

summary.trap: Reading “$A$ or $B$” as “exactly one of them” leaves out the overlap, where both happen.

quiz.prose: Over 50 trading days, signal X fired on 18 days and signal Y on 14. Both fired on 6 of those days.
quiz.question: What fraction of the days had X or Y firing? Give a fraction or a decimal.

widget.label: Share of days with X or Y

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the two counts, then take the overlap away once.

byKey.double: You added 18 and 14. The 6 days with both were counted twice.
byKey.xor: You left out the 6 days with both. “Or” includes them.
byKey.and: That is the share with both signals.

explain.text: $|X \cup Y| = 18 + 14 - 6 = 26$ days. So the share is $\tfrac{26}{50} = 0.52$.

quiz.prose: $A$ and $B$ are two events in the same sample space.
quiz.question: Which set is “neither $A$ nor $B$”?

options.why: That is “not both”. It also holds outcomes in exactly one of $A$ and $B$.
That is “not both” again, the same as $A^c \cup B^c$.
That is $B$ without $A$. Neither means outside $B$ as well.

feedback.correct: Outside the union: $(A \cup B)^c = A^c \cap B^c$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Neither means outside both circles.

explain.text: Neither $A$ nor $B$ means outside both circles. That is the complement of the union, $(A \cup B)^c$, which De Morgan also writes as $A^c \cap B^c$.

quiz.prose: A stock closes up, flat or down. $P(\text{up}) = 0.45$ and $P(\text{down}) = 0.4$. Up and down are disjoint.
quiz.question: What is $P(\text{flat})$? Give a decimal.

feedback.correct: Flat is the complement of up or down: $1 - 0.85$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find $P(\text{up or down})$ first.

byKey.up-or-down: That is $P(\text{up or down})$. Flat is everything else.
byKey.not-up: That is $P(\text{not up})$, which includes down days.
byKey.not-down: That is $P(\text{not down})$, which includes up days.

explain.text: Up and down share no outcome, so $P(\text{up or down}) = 0.45 + 0.4 = 0.85$. Flat is the complement of that union. So $P(\text{flat}) = 1 - 0.85 = 0.15$.

quiz.prose: Two fair dice. $A$: the total is 10 or more, 6 rolls. $B$: a double, 6 rolls.
quiz.question: What is $P(A \cup B)$? Give a fraction or a decimal.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the rolls in both events first.

byKey.double: You added 6 and 6. (5, 5) and (6, 6) are in both, so they were counted twice.
byKey.xor: You left out (5, 5) and (6, 6), the rolls in both.

explain.text: The doubles with a total of 10 or more are (5, 5) and (6, 6), so $|A \cap B| = 2$. Then $|A \cup B| = 6 + 6 - 2 = 10$. So $P(A \cup B) = \tfrac{10}{36} = \tfrac{5}{18}$.
